headline: Overnight I-95 closures begin at Providence-Cranston Route 10 interchange
dek: RIDOT will close I-95 in both directions around midnight on Oct. 16 and 17, with three weekends of changing restrictions and Route 10 ramp detours ahead.
body: Late-night drivers using the I-95 and Route 10 interchange in Providence and Cranston should plan for major disruptions beginning Friday, Oct. 16. The Rhode Island Department of Transportation says a three-weekend sequence of bridge-demolition work will bring lane restrictions, full overnight closures and several closed Route 10 ramps around Exit 33. The first weekend is the most restrictive: both directions of I-95 are scheduled to close at midnight on the nights of Oct. 16 and 17.

RIDOT’s schedule separates the first weekend’s early lane reductions from the full shutdown. Up to two lanes in each direction may close by 10 p.m., followed by a complete closure at midnight. Southbound I-95 is scheduled to reopen by 5 a.m. the next morning, while northbound is scheduled to reopen by 7 a.m. Those are construction targets rather than guarantees; the department says project schedules can change because of weather, field conditions or work requirements. The [RIDOT travel advisory](https://www.ri.gov/press/view/51514) is the controlling source for the published timetable.

Three Route 10 connections are also scheduled to close from 10 p.m. to 5 a.m. on each of the affected Friday and Saturday nights: Route 10 South to I-95 North, Route 10 North to I-95 South, and I-95 South to Route 10 South. That means some trips will encounter a ramp closure before the interstate itself fully shuts down. For the first weekend, RIDOT directs southbound travelers to leave at Exit 33B for Route 10 North, use Exit 2A for Reservoir Avenue and follow the signed route back toward Route 10 South. Northbound travelers can use Exit 33A to Route 10 North or the Elmwood Avenue alternative from Exit 33B, depending on their trip.

The next two weekends will not repeat the first weekend exactly. On the nights of Oct. 23 and 24, I-95 South is scheduled for a full midnight closure and reopening by 7 a.m., while northbound traffic is limited to closures of the two left lanes. On Oct. 30 and 31, RIDOT lists up to two southbound lanes closed by 10 p.m. and three southbound lanes closed at midnight; the published plan lists no northbound lane closure for that weekend. The same three Route 10 ramp closures are scheduled from 10 p.m. to 5 a.m. across the series.

RIDOT estimates that detour trips could take 15 to 20 minutes longer, with the greatest travel times expected in the morning before lanes reopen. The agency recommends considering I-295 or Route 10 as alternate routes and checking its current travel advisories before leaving. Independent Rhode Island reporting by [UpriseRI](https://upriseri.com/article/i-95-to-close-overnight-at-route-10-starting-oct-16/) likewise describes the first weekend as a full closure in both directions followed by narrower restrictions on the next two weekends, while noting that the schedule is subject to change.

The closures are part of RIDOT’s I-95 15 Bridges project, which is rebuilding the Route 10 interchange and addressing 15 bridges along the I-95 and Route 10 corridor between Providence and Warwick. The [project page](https://dot.ri.gov/projects/The-I-95-15/index.php) says the corridor carries about 185,000 vehicles daily, including roughly 9,000 trucks and other heavy-freight vehicles. RIDOT lists a projected project cost of $779 million, a construction period running from 2024 through 2031 and a $251 million federal Bridge Investment Program grant.

For residents traveling between Providence, Cranston, Warwick and nearby communities, the practical issue is not only whether I-95 is open but which direction and connection a trip uses. A driver who relies on one of the three Route 10 ramps can face a separate 10 p.m. closure even when through lanes remain available. A northbound trip during the first weekend may also require waiting until the 7 a.m. reopening target, two hours later than the scheduled southbound reopening. Travelers should follow the signs in place, allow extra time and verify the latest RIDOT notice before each overnight trip.

The first restrictions begin Friday evening, but they are not a continuous two-day shutdown: the full closures are scheduled for the overnight periods leading into Saturday and Sunday mornings. The later October weekends have different lane patterns, so motorists should not assume that the first weekend’s complete closure will recur. RIDOT’s detour maps and travel-advisory page remain the best places to check for updates as demolition work proceeds.
location: I-95 and Route 10 interchange, Providence and Cranston, Rhode Island
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Overnight I-95 closures begin Oct. 16 at Rhode Island Route 10
seoDescription: RIDOT will close I-95 in both directions overnight at the Route 10 interchange in Providence and Cranston on Oct. 16 and 17, followed by two weekends of changing restrictions.
